text:
The cyberpunk metropolis, known historically as Neo-Veridia, was not merely a city but a vertical ecosystem engineered for efficiency and surveillance. Its history dates back to the Great Data Collapse of the late 21st century, when traditional power grids failed and corporate conglomerates seized control of the remaining infrastructure. The skyscrapers, constructed from carbon-nanotube reinforced glass and self-healing concrete, rose like jagged teeth against the smog-choked sky. These structures were not just offices but entire worlds, connected by sky-bridges and magnetic transit tubes, creating a layered society where the wealthy lived in the sun-drenched upper spires and the poor navigated the perpetual twilight of the street level.

The neon glow that defined the city was not just aesthetic; it was a byproduct of the massive server farms cooling systems and the holographic advertisements that projected directly into the retinas of passersby via augmented reality implants. The streets below were a chaotic tapestry of steam vents, rain-slicked asphalt, and the relentless hum of hovercars weaving through narrow canyons of steel and light. Digital billboards, omnipresent and unblinking, did not just sell products; they monitored mood, purchasing power, and social credit scores, adjusting their content in real-time to manipulate consumer behavior. This constant churn of humanity was a mix of desperate laborers, tech-runners, and corporate elites, all bound together by the city’s central AI, which watched every move with cold, algorithmic precision.

Amidst this high-tech, low-life environment, the primary material of a traditional candle remains beeswax. In a world dominated by synthetic polymers and electric light, beeswax is a rare commodity, harvested from the few remaining organic apiaries located in the sealed, climate-controlled domes of the upper city. It is prized not for its utility, as electric lights are far more efficient, but for its symbolic value. The slow, steady burn of beeswax represents a connection to a pre-digital, natural past, offering a flickering, organic warmth that contrasts sharply with the harsh, static glare of the neon metropolis.
